title: No first-class Rust crate-extraction facility (monolith → workspace-member crate)
wanted_capability:
A reusable way to extract a cohesive subsystem out of a monolithic crate into a new workspace-member crate, as a guarded/transactional operation. Concretely: (1) scaffold the new crate — create crates/<name>/Cargo.toml ([package] + inferred [dependencies]) and src/lib.rs, add <name> to the root [workspace].members, and add <name> = { path = "crates/<name>" } to each named consumer's [dependencies]; (2) move the chosen modules/items into it with visibility bumped to pub at the new crate boundary; (3) crate-aware path rewrite — rewrite `crate::<seg>` / `use crate::<seg>` references in the origin crate to `<new_crate>::<seg>` (with use-tree splitting), and rewrite references from the extracted code back into the origin to `<origin_crate>::...`; (4) DAG guard — verify the extraction keeps the workspace dependency graph acyclic (this repo's contract-bottom invariant: implementation crates point down, never sideways/up); (5) validate via cargo check --workspace + rust_compile_fix_round with rollback across all writes. Ideal shape is a compound bbox_refactor_run macro `extract_rust_crate`, directly analogous to the existing `migrate_rust_mods_to_lib` macro but one level out (package→new-package instead of bin→lib), optionally fronted by a refactor atom for autonomous repeat use.</wanted_capability>
<parameter name="missing_primitive">A `extract_rust_crate` compound plan/macro (bbox_refactor_run) plus its three missing sub-primitives: a workspace-crate scaffolder (Cargo.toml + lib.rs + members + consumer dep-edge wiring), a crate-aware path rewriter (`crate::`/`use crate::` ↔ `<crate>::` with use-tree splitting, generalizing rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths beyond the bin→lib case), and a workspace-DAG acyclicity check.</missing_primitive>
<parameter name="fallback_used">Hand-compose the sequence from existing within-crate primitives: write_file + multiple ensure_toml_table for scaffolding and dep wiring; rust_top_level_dependency_analysis to find the seam; extract_rust_items_to_submodule / move_rust_items_with_local_deps to move the cluster; migrate_rust_mods_to_lib / rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths / move_rust_items_with_callers approximate the path rewrite (simple-name-segment match only, not crate-path aware, no use-tree splitting — leftovers need manual cleanup); rewrite_rust_*_visibility for the pub bump; bbox_refactor_run with cargo gates + rust_compile_fix_round to converge. No DAG cycle guard exists; relies on cargo check failing.</fallback_used>

crates/bbox-vectors/ — worked example: src/vectors hand-extracted 2026-06-08, surfaced the cfg(test)/dep-enumeration/re-export findings below
notes:
Motivated by the ~15m release build: the 277k-LOC root `blackbox` crate is the serial-frontend bottleneck, so peeling cold subsystems (refactor/, workflow/, macros/, knowledge-graph) into their own crates is a recurring, ongoing need — not a one-shot. The migrate_rust_mods_to_lib macro already proves the transactional shape (copy mod decls → delete from origin → rewrite crate:: paths → check every bin → fix-round → final cargo check); extract_rust_crate is that pattern generalized to arbitrary crate boundaries plus a scaffolder and a DAG guard. The DAG guard is repo-specific-valuable here because the harness↔daemon boundary is compiler-enforced acyclic (bro-harness must never depend on blackbox); a crate-extraction tool that can introduce a cycle would violate a documented invariant silently until link time.

=== Findings from the 2026-06-08 hand-extraction of src/vectors → bbox-vectors (a textbook zero-coupling leaf, yet it still needed four non-obvious fixups the facility must automate) ===

1. DEP ENUMERATION must scan inline-qualified paths, not just `use` statements, and must split test/dev-only deps. A `use`-only scan missed `dirs::home_dir()` (inline, non-test → [dependencies]) and `tempfile::` (used only under #[cfg(test)] → [dev-dependencies]). The scaffolder must collect every `<root>::` first segment across all files (minus std/core/alloc/self/super/crate + the crate's own submodules), resolve versions from the parent manifest, and route test-only-used crates to [dev-dependencies]. The compiler drove both fixups here — the facility should pre-compute them.

2. cfg(test) ITEMS CONSUMED ACROSS THE NEW BOUNDARY need a `test-support` feature. #[cfg(test)] does not cross crate boundaries: a dependency is always built non-test, so test-support helpers (here install_test_global / TestGlobalStoreGuard / test_global_store) that the PARENT crate's tests call simply vanish. Fix pattern: (a) detect cfg(test) items referenced from outside the extracted module's own #[cfg(test)] tests; (b) convert their gate AND every read-path that uses them to `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` (missing the read-path inside global()/try_global() would compile but silently not consult the installed test store); (c) add `[features] test-support = []` to the child; (d) wire the parent's `[dev-dependencies] <child> = { path=..., features=["test-support"] }` so the feature is on only for the parent's tests, off in release (zero hot-path cost). Resolver v2/v3 keeps the dev-dep feature out of normal builds.

3. LOW-COLLISION CALLER REWRITE: aliasing the child back under the old module path in the parent lib.rs (`use bbox_vectors as vectors;`) makes every existing `crate::vectors::*` call site resolve unchanged — 1 line touched instead of editing N caller files. On shared/hot branches this is strictly better than the crate-aware path rewriter (no churn in peer-owned files). The facility should offer the re-export alias as the DEFAULT strategy and the path-rewrite as the opt-in (when you actually want call sites to name the new crate). Note privacy: a private `use child as oldmod;` at the crate root is visible to the whole crate (root's descendants), matching the original private `mod oldmod;`.

4. pub(crate) PROMOTION is selective: free fns/types reached across the boundary go pub (iter_active/active_entity_hashes/cluster_neighbors_within_route), but same-named inherent methods that are only called internally stay pub(crate). A blind pub(crate)->pub sweep would over-expose; the facility must promote only the items in the actual external-reference set.

Net: even the cleanest possible extraction (zero blackbox deps) needed dep-enum + cfg(test)-feature + selective-pub + self-path-rewrite. A naive "move files + add to workspace" would have failed all four. validation: cargo check (non-test) clean, cargo check -p bbox-vectors --features test-support clean, cargo check --tests clean, 21/21 moved unit tests pass.
